text:
Maya (PM): Heads-up — getting pressure from three pilot customers asking for per-tenant routing policies + tenant-scoped audit trails. Sales wants this in the next sprint for pilots. Quick sync?

Raj (GTM): +1. Customers say 'we need to route certain traffic to private models or higher tier pools per tenant'. Pilot timelines slipping without it.

Sam (Sales): For context, Acme and Beacon said they'd sign pilots if we can guarantee tenant-level control and logs for compliance. They asked for a 'pilot-ready' path not a full platform rewrite.

Emily (Eng): We can do a pragmatic shim: a per-tenant static routing config that maps tenant -> route, stored in config service. Fast to ship (1 sprint + small canary) but no UI/rollout controls and brittle for scale.

Lena (Research): Long-term we want a policy engine (conditions, TTL, rollout) so tenants can mutate routing without ops. That is a 2–3 sprint build with evals on perf and cache behavior.

Chris (Data): Key metrics to validate: 95th pct tail latency delta, per-tenant cost delta, and traceability (audit log completeness). We should define gating thresholds now.

Maya (PM): Proposal: present three options to execs & sales:
A) Quick shim: static tenant routing + 90d audit logs retained (pilot friendly).
B) Policy engine MVP: rule-based routing + rollout hooks (medium effort).
C) Temporary managed offering: Dedicated capacity + hand-off ops for pilot customers (lowest product change, requires infra/ops).

Emily (Eng): Tradeoffs: A = ~2 devs for 2 weeks + 1 oncall for rollout. B = ~4 devs 6–8 weeks, infra changes for policy evaluation path. C = ops burden + commit for Dedicated pools, SLA negotiation.

Sam (Sales): For pilot signups, Acme will accept A if we pair with a documented deprecation path and a paid support SLA. Beacon prefers C but could do A if we promise fast follow-up.

Raj (GTM): Can we scope A to be non-breaking for B later? I.e., use same config keys so we can migrate tenants to policy engine without DB reshuffle.

Emily (Eng): Yes — implement A as a routing layer that reads tenant config from the config service; policy engine can later augment/override that namespace. Keep schema stable.

Maya (PM): Launch criteria for A (pilot):
- End-to-end routing for tenant X to alternate pool verified in canary.
- 95th percentile latency increase <= 10% on affected routes.
- Audit logs capture request id + tenant + resolved route and persisted for 90 days.
- Product sign-off + sales commitment doc for pilot.

Chris (Data): We'll add a lightweight smoke eval to measure token throughput and cost delta per tenant for two weeks post-rollout.

Lena (Research): Also flag: KV cache behavior may change if tenants hit different model variants. We should instrument cache hit rates per tenant to detect regressions.

Maya (PM): Decision needed: Do we greenlight A for next sprint as a tactical pilot shim (with migration path) or push to policy engine MVP? Vote please (react with :+1: for A, :shrug: for B, :-1: for C).

Emily (Eng): :+1: (A with migration path).

Sam (Sales): :+1: (A to close pilots).

Raj (GTM): :+1: (A, urgent).

Lena (Research): :shrug: (prefer B long-term but ok).

Chris (Data): :+1: (A if we instrument properly).

Maya (PM): Great — I'll write a tight spec for A with the launch criteria above and schedule a short spike to validate config schema. Action items:
- Maya: spec + rollout runbook by EOD tomorrow.
- Emily: estimate & spike for config read path (2 days).
- Chris: draft smoke eval and instrumentation fields.
- Sam: capture pilot commitment language and expected close dates.

deploy-bot: New doc created: https://redwood.atlassian.com/PLAT-2345 - "Tenant routing shim (pilot)"

Raj (GTM): Thanks — keep me looped, I want to present this in the pilot sync on Friday.

Maya (PM): Will do. If anyone has objections to scope or unacceptable risk items, flag here. Otherwise we'll roll with A into the next sprint planning. :rocket:
